newsitem.title: USA: US corporate debt mart quiet, tobacco tightens.
newsitem.headline: US corporate debt mart quiet, tobacco tightens.

text.p: In the corporate bond high-grade sector, spreads of tobacco debt tightened on news of talks between tobacco executives and state attorneys general in an otherwise quiet market, dealers said.
In the broader secondary market, spreads to Treasuries remained unchanged across most maturiites, they said.

News of negotiations on a possible settlement of massive tobacco industry litigation triggered RJR Nabisco's debt to tighten by five to ten basis points. RJR paper due 2005 was quoted at 205 basis points bid, 200 basis points offered, traders said.
Pressure had been steadily building on the tobacco industry to seek a resolution to mounting lawsuits and other legal developments against it.
"Tobacco debt was tighter today, specifically, the longer paper," said one high-grade trader.
Philip Morris' 7.20 percent 10-year paper was quoted tighter by about three basis points at 85 bid, 80 offer, and the firm's debt due 2027 was seen 100 basis points bid, traders said.
Shorter-dated tobacco paper was seen a touch tighter to unchanged, traders said.
Philip Morris' 7-1/2s of 2002 were quoted 68 basis points bid, 63 offer. RJR's 8-5/8's of 2002 were trading at a 170 basis point bid, while the 7.625's of 2003 were bid at 195.
Meanwhile, the corporate bond primary sector saw various issuers tap the market as the tone in the U.S. Treasury market improved, syndicate sources said.

Among the issuers were Food Lion issued $150 million in 7.55 percent 10-year notes to yield 72 basis points over Treasuries and $150 million in 8.05 percent 30-year debentures to yield 95 basis points. Salomon Brothers was lead underwriter for the offering.

In addition, General Motors Corp unit, General Motors Acceptance Corp (GMAC), set $1.0 billion in a five-year floating rate note issue to yield 12.5 basis points over the three-month libor rate. The deal was underwritten by joint lead managers Morgan Stanley & Co and UBS Securities Inc.
Turning to the high-yield sector, supermarket paper weakened in an otherwise very inactive market, traders said.
Volume is expected to remain light as most players attend industry conferences held in Arizona and New York City this week, players said.
"Across the baord there's doesn't seem to be a lot of activity as so many people are out at conferences," said one high-yield trader.
Meanwhile, Grand Union's 12 percent debt was off 1/2 to 95-1/2 bid. Pathmark debt also weakended 1/2 to trade at 93-1/4 bid, 93-3/4 offer, traders said.
